summary: Bumps the exact pin of @cipherstash/protect-ffi from 0.30.0 to 0.31.0 (a release with breaking changes) and adapts @cipherstash/stack to it: error-code detection moves from `instanceof ProtectError` to a value check (`isProtectErrorCode`), the WASM `newClient` call moves credentials into `clientOpts` and renames `strategy` to `authStrategy`, the WASM entry stops pre-normalising `cast_as`, and the bulk/model paths strip the stack-side correlation `id` that 0.31 now rejects. The most material release consequence is intended and loud: an explicitly supplied base64 `clientKey` / `CS_CLIENT_KEY` now fails at client construction, which the change handles with a major changeset, skill documentation and a CI hex pre-check. The main open question is that the native `newClient` call (unchanged, packages/stack/src/encryption/index.ts) still passes the auth strategy under the old `strategy` key, which commit comments describe as a deprecated alias in 0.31; whether the native entry honours it could not be checked because the 0.31 package is not available here. Unit tests target every adapted seam but mock the FFI, and no test results were seen.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack's runtime dependency on @cipherstash/protect-ffi moves from 0.30.0 to 0.31.0 (exact pin), including all six per-platform native binaries; stack-drizzle and stack-supabase dev pins follow.

An explicitly supplied `clientKey` (config or CS_CLIENT_KEY) must now be hex; a base64 key that 0.30 accepted is rejected at client construction with a deliberately terse error. This is a behaviour change inherited from protect-ffi, declared as a major bump of @cipherstash/stack.

`getErrorCode` and DynamoDB `handleError` now report a code only when its value is in protect-ffi's known code set. Previously `handleError` passed through any string `code` (e.g. ECONNRESET); now such errors surface as DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR, and `getErrorCode` returns undefined for them.

WASM entry `Encryption` passes `authStrategy` (was `strategy`) and nests `clientId`/`clientKey` under `clientOpts`; the `as never` cast is removed so the options are type-checked against 0.31 declarations; `encryptConfig` is passed without `normalizeCastAs`, relying on 0.31 to canonicalise `cast_as` in Rust.
Bulk encrypt/decrypt operations and all eight model helpers no longer forward the stack-side correlation `id` across the FFI boundary; results continue to be correlated by array position.
The shared `require-cs-secrets` CI action now fails a job when CS_CLIENT_KEY is not an even-length hex string, without echoing the key.
The bundled `stash-auth` agent skill (shipped to customer repos) gains guidance that CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex, with recovery advice per entry point.

failure_scenarios.title: Native entry passes the auth strategy under the pre-0.31 `strategy` key
failure_scenarios.trigger: A native-entry caller supplies `config.authStrategy` (e.g. an OidcFederationStrategy for user-scoped, identity-bound encryption) and protect-ffi 0.31's Neon entry does not honour `strategy` as an alias of `authStrategy`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: encryption/index.ts still calls `newClient({ ..., strategy: config.authStrategy, eqlVersion: 3 })`. The same change renames the WASM option to `authStrategy`, and its own comments say both entries now deserialize the same `NewClientOptions` and that `strategy` survives only as a deprecated alias. If the alias is missing or ignored on the native entry, the strategy is dropped silently and the client builds a default AutoStrategy from env/profile credentials.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Requests authenticate as the service credential rather than the end-user strategy; identity-bound operations either fail or run under the wrong identity. If the alias is present (as the commit claims for wasm), nothing happens.

existing_verification.description: init-strategy.test.ts asserts the strategy reaches a mocked newClient as `opts.strategy`; it pins stack's call shape, not what 0.31 accepts.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Pass `authStrategy` on the native call too (it is the current name per this change), or verify the alias in the 0.31 package and add a live assertion that getToken is invoked.

failure_scenarios.title: Deployments with a base64 clientKey fail at client construction after upgrade
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer upgrades @cipherstash/stack with CS_CLIENT_KEY or config.clientKey copied in base64 form (e.g. from ~/.cipherstash/secretkey.json).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The exact pin forces protect-ffi 0.31.0, whose explicit-clientKey decoder is hex-only; the error message omits the cause by design. On wasm-inline there is no profile-store fallback.
failure_scenarios.consequence: All encryption and decryption fail for that deployment until the key is re-encoded; loud, no data effect, recoverable by config change or rollback to the previous major.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Already mitigated by a major version bump, the changeset upgrade note and the stash-auth skill guidance. Release notes should lead with it.

failure_scenarios.title: DynamoDB/operation callers branching on error.code see different codes
failure_scenarios.trigger: A caller of the DynamoDB helpers branches on `error.code` values that were foreign (ECONNRESET, AWS SDK codes) or on a code the FFI emits that is not in isProtectErrorCode's set.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: handleError now maps any code not accepted by `isProtectErrorCode` to DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR, and getErrorCode returns undefined for it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Retry/fail logic keyed on transport codes stops matching; the intended outcome is that transport faults are no longer mislabelled as encryption faults. Loud only if callers notice.

existing_verification.description: New unit tests for handleError (resolve-decrypt.test.ts) and getErrorCode (error-helpers.test.ts) cover foreign and known codes against the real predicate.

missing_verification: Nothing shows every code 0.31 actually throws is in `isProtectErrorCode`'s set (the predicate is protect-ffi's own, which reduces the risk).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Documented in the changeset; no further action beyond review.

failure_scenarios.title: A remaining FFI call path still carries a key 0.31 rejects
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any bulk/model/query payload sent to protect-ffi 0.31 that contains an undeclared top-level key.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: 0.31 forwards unknown keys to Rust, which rejects the whole call. The change strips `id` in bulk-encrypt, bulk-decrypt and all eight model helpers; query paths build explicit payloads. The native model-helper strip has no unit test; only live integration suites exercise it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every model/bulk operation on an unpatched path fails loudly (no wrong data).
